cases.feature_description: User login with username and password, including invalid credentials and account lockout after repeated failed attempts.
Self-service password reset via an emailed reset link, including expired links and links that have already been used once.
Exporting a test suite's test cases and each one's latest run status to a CSV file, including suites that have zero test cases.
Creating, renaming, and deleting a project. Only an admin user may perform these actions; a non-admin (viewer) must be rejected.
Filtering a suite's test case list by priority (low, medium, high, critical) and by status, including a filter combination that matches nothing.
Computing a completed test run's pass/fail/skip percentages, including the edge case of a run with zero recorded results (must not divide by zero).
Selecting an execution environment (staging, regression, preprod, prod) when starting a test run, including what happens when an unrecognised environment key is supplied.
Paginated project listing with an optional search query parameter, including a search term that matches no project and a page number past the last page.
Bulk-selecting multiple test suites within a project and deleting them in one action, including a partial failure where one selected suite has already been deleted by another admin.
Live test run status pushed to every connected browser over a WebSocket connection as results are recorded, including a client that disconnects mid-run and must resync its state on reconnect.

Role-based access control across every write action (create, edit, delete) for suites, test cases and runs: an admin may perform all of them, a viewer may perform none and must receive a 403 response for each attempt.

The AI test-case generation endpoint that turns a feature description into draft test cases, including the case where no AI API key is configured (must return a clean 503, never a crash) and the case where the model's response is not valid JSON (must return a 502 with a clear error, never leak the raw response).
Publishing a run-completion event to a Kafka topic when a test run finishes, and the consumer processing that event idempotently so a redelivered message does not double-count the run's stats.

The guest-facing demo-seed endpoint that creates a flagship demo project on first use: clicking the same demo button repeatedly, refreshing mid-seed, and two guests seeding at nearly the same moment must never result in more than one flagship demo project existing.

The public contact form: a valid submission with topic, email and description; a submission missing a required field; an invalid email format; and repeated rapid submissions from the same visitor that should be rate-limited rather than all accepted.
